details.detail: Screen wall and screen proportion. The screen size is correct at 0.952 x 0.535, but it sits too low in a wall that is too tall. The taupe band plus cap above the screen measures 0.14 m in the render (q03 crop: 90 px against a 350 px screen height). In real photos it is 0.044 m (omaat_11: 28 px of 635 px/m) and 0.058 m (omaat_32: 30 px against a 275 px screen). Seat back to wall top shows the same thing: 0.22 m in the model against about 0.12 m in omaat_9.

Centre wood between the D and G screens. The w4 solid half-wedges mirror into a thick V that is open at the aft end and reaches H = 1.30. From the aisle (q02 x415-495 y130-310) it reads as a folded book or a square wood pillar with a crease. In reality it is ONE flat wood board in the divider plane (the fixed forward section of the movable divider). It has a thin taupe frame on its aft and top edges, its top is level with the screen top (below the rim), and it runs about 0.30 m aft. See omaat_32 (same viewpoint as q02), omaat_5 (seen face-on from the G side), and tlfl_14 (divider raised: the fin is the forward panel behind a taupe frame member).

Aisle pier, pill mirror and reading lamp. Placement and pier width are good against omaat_11. The mirror renders too light: #74849b in q03 against #58637d in omaat_11. It reads as a lit panel rather than a dark reflection.

Window wing and the shelf at the forward end of the console. The wing is fine. The small taupe shelf (0.12 x 0.02 at y 0.70) floats about 0.025 m above the console rail, with a visible shadow gap (q03 x340-385 y320-335). The real one (omaat_11 x825-945 y400-460, omaat_27, omaat_58) is a solid block the width of the console, sitting on it, with a dark-wood top level with the table.

Dining table (stowed), ottoman and aisle box. Proportions match omaat_11: table 0.72 x 0.20 with a black lip, cantilevered cushion over a dark void, and the box top level with the table. The ottoman colour is good (render #726a61 against real #7e6f68).

Window console, tray, keypad and handset. Order is correct: handset aft, keypad forward, tray further forward. The real tray is a sculpted curved swoosh recess that rises at its forward end (omaat_5, tlfl_14), not a flat tapered inlay. This is acceptable at cabin distance.

Seat, headrest flap, pillow and niche. Geometry is good: the flap is 78 % of the back width against 76 % real, and 0.20 high against 28 % of the back. There is too large a gap between the back top (about 1.14) and the header (1.20-1.30); in omaat_9 the back tucks directly under a header about 0.11 tall. In s4 the flap renders darker than the back (#5d5e59 against #68606b, ratio 0.94). Real photos show it 1.16-1.40x lighter and neutral: omaat_2 #5d5e59/#49413e, omaat_8 #7e7d7c/#5f5b57, jsh_2 #646464/#46403b. The real back has 3 channel seams, the model has 2.

Aisle exterior. The fluted leaves, frames, LED kick line and silver pulls read well (15-rib pitch accepted). The aft 0.38 m of the wardrobe's aisle face (z -0.46 to -0.08) is a dark-wood panel. In every real aisle photo the whole aisle face is fluted from the plaque end forward (omaat_7 and omaat_58 right-hand units, omaat_40, jsh_2); the wood only appears on the wardrobe's INNER face.

Caps and the forward corner arm. The arm reads correctly from the aisle side. From the seat (q03 x700-840 y85-130) it is still a long rounded bolster whose inboard end overhangs the pier. On the aisle, the real cap has a thicker front face (about 0.09 against 0.06 in the model).

Centre divider (lowered). The height and the taupe rail are consistent with omaat_5 and omaat_2. Real photos also show a dark-wood band just below the taupe top rail, running the full length (omaat_5 x80-960 y640-680).

Bed mode. The pillows are right: white pillow upright, lavender lying low. The duvet is a narrower raised slab offset to the window side, so it reads as a second mattress (q04). The real duvet (omaat_57/58/59) covers the full pad width, drapes over both edges and the foot, and has a turned-down diagonal corner and soft folds. Sun stripes are out of scope.

Seat plaque. In q02, 2G is a large navy box with a grey border on the aft cap. The real plaque (omaat_40 '1G', omaat_9 '2K') is a small (~0.06 x 0.035) recessed taupe rounded rectangle with glowing blue-white text at the cap corner.

Artefacts. No z-fighting, clipping or moire found in these frames. The only floating part is the console shelf. The pink hand-shaped patch in q02 (x150-190 y330-370) is a sun patch (lighting, out of scope). Also out of scope: window sun stripes on the bed.

issues.issue: Centre pair: the wood between the D and G screens is a thick V-wedge pillar that reaches the wall top. It should be one thin flat board in the divider plane with its top at the screen top.
issues.evidence: q02_suiteAisle.png x415-495 y130-310: two 18-deg slabs read as a folded book or pillar, colour #2f2420. omaat_32.jpg (same viewpoint): one flat wood board with a thin taupe edge; its top (y~365) is level with the 2G screen top (y~375) and well below the rim (y~345); it runs about 0.30 m aft (110 px in x against a 385 px screen). omaat_5.jpg x990-1200 y365-680: flat board, wood #42372d, taupe frame on the aft and top edges. tlfl_14.jpg: with the divider raised the fin is the divider's forward panel behind a taupe frame member.
issues.fix: In suiteUnit's center branch (line 62), replace the gExtrude wedge with an in-plane half board. Each mirrored unit builds its own half: B.add(gRBox(0.015, 1.24 - 0.62, 0.30, 0.004, 1), M4.trs(-hx + 0.0075, 0.62 + (1.24 - 0.62)/2, -L + 0.12 + 0.15), SEATMAT.fWood). Taupe frame: B.add(gRBox(0.016, 0.02, 0.30, 0.004, 1), M4.trs(-hx + 0.008, 1.25, -L + 0.27), SEATMAT.fDoor) on top, and B.add(gRBox(0.016, 1.25 - 0.62, 0.02, 0.004, 1), M4.trs(-hx + 0.008, 0.62 + (1.25 - 0.62)/2, -L + 0.41), SEATMAT.fDoor) on the aft edge. Keep the top at about 1.25 (screen top + 0.02), not H. If the screen is raised (next issue), use board top = screen top + 0.02.

issues.issue: The screen wall rises 0.14 m above the screen. Real walls rise about 0.05 m (the screen fills the wall to just under the rim), and the aft header stands about 0.22 m above the seat back against about 0.12 m in reality. The whole shell top is about 0.07-0.09 m too high relative to the screen and the seat.
issues.evidence: q03_suite1A.png: 90 px of taupe above the screen against a 350 px screen height, i.e. 0.14 m. omaat_11.jpg: rim 28 px against a screen width of 605 px = 0.952 m, i.e. 0.044 m. omaat_32.jpg: 30 px against a 275 px screen height, i.e. 0.058 m. omaat_9.jpg: header about 0.11 m and back top almost touching it. Model: back top about 1.14, header 1.20-1.30, cap top 1.3625. jsh_0.jpg: the seated passenger's head top is about level with the wall rim.
issues.fix: Change H to 1.24 in suiteUnit (line 23) and suiteFar (line 253), so the cap top is 1.3025. Raise the screen centre from 0.95 to 0.98 (bezel line 50, quad line 51, suiteFar 0.93 -> 0.96): top 1.2475, leaving 0.055 of rim above it. Raise the table 0.02 to keep its 0.035 gap under the screen (line 80 y 0.625 -> 0.645, lip line 81 0.60 -> 0.62, PULL tab 0.60 -> 0.62) and the aisle box top by the same amount (line 86 0.61 -> 0.63). Change the niche header (line 215) to height 0.08 at y H - 0.04, and spot y from H - 0.05 to H - 0.04. Pier spot (line 76) y 1.20 -> 1.16. The wing, pier and wardrobe heights follow H automatically. If H must stay at 1.30 for privacy reasons, the alternative is screen centre 1.03 with the table at 0.70, but that puts the table high.

issues.issue: The wardrobe's aisle face carries a 0.38 m dark-wood panel. In real photos the whole aisle face is fluted (the wood is only on the inner face).
issues.evidence: s6_suiteW_aisle.png x55-135: dark-wood panel beside the fluted leaf. omaat_7.jpg (2K unit x800-1150) and omaat_58.jpg (2K x800-1180) are fluted continuously from the plaque (aft) end forward. omaat_40.jpg 1G and jsh_2.jpg x950-1500 show no wood on the aisle side. Real leaf colour in cabin light: #2c2e20 in omaat_58 (dim) against #6b5e4e in the s6 render.
issues.fix: Lines 193-196: replace the fWood gBox (z -0.27, 0.32 long) with the same rib run used for the leaves. Extend the aft leaf loop to [z0, z1] = [-0.96, -0.08] with its own fFluteGap backing and 15-per-0.5 m pitch (0.026), or add a second run [-0.46, -0.08] with the stile/rail frames at lines 187-188. Keep the LED line.

issues.issue: The bed duvet is a narrow raised slab and reads as a second mattress. The real duvet covers the full width and drapes over the edges and the foot.
issues.evidence: q04_suite1Abed.png y200-350: a white slab (#dad8d5) with a crisp rounded outline sitting on the white pad. omaat_58.jpg / omaat_57.jpg: the duvet covers the whole pad from console to armrest, hangs about 0.10 over the aisle edge and the foot, has a diagonal turned-down corner at the aisle-side top, and soft folds.
issues.fix: Line 222: duvet width SW * 0.62 -> SW + 0.04, centred at seatX - 0.01 (the pad centre), thickness 0.07 -> 0.035, y 0.50 -> 0.485. Add drape skirts: B.add(gRBox(0.012, 0.09, 1.40, 0.006, 1), M4.trs(seatX - 0.01 +/- (SW/2 + 0.026), 0.44, -1.20), duv) on both sides, plus a foot skirt gRBox(SW + 0.05, 0.10, 0.012) at z -2.07, y 0.43. Replace the full-width fold (line 226) with a triangular turned-down corner: gExtrude([[0,0],[0.30,0],[0,0.30]], 0.012) on the aisle side at z -0.55, y 0.505, colour 0.96x the duvet.

questions: Is the 1.30 m shell height sourced? It is [A] in REFERENCE777.md. Two independent measurements (screen rim in omaat_11 / omaat_32, and header over the seat back in omaat_9) both point to a cap top of about 1.28-1.30 rather than 1.36. Lowering H is the cleanest fix, but it changes privacy in every view.

The w3/w4 raters modelled the centre wood as an angled V (from omaat_f3/f4). My downloads of the same OMAAT set (omaat_32, omaat_5, omaat_33) plus tlfl_14 show a single flat board in the divider plane. Can the integrator confirm with the old ref/web/suite/omaat_f3 file before the fixer changes it?
Aisle face of the wardrobe: w1 cited pb_20 for wood flanks. Every OMAAT, JSH and TLFL aisle photo I found is fully fluted. Is pb_20 perhaps a closed-door view from inside?
